I'd love to have a chance.” He at least is in all the majors next year from his 2023 British Open victory at Hoylake. Going into the final day, Im is the only player projected to move into the top 50 — he started at No. 53 and held his own in the final group Saturday with Scheffler. “I just want to focus on each shot,” Im said. “Every shot matters.” Scheffler only hit one green in regulation through the opening five holes. He was in the right rough on the par-5 third and had a clean enough lie to try to reach the green or at least advance it close. But it hit a tree right above him and dropped straight down. He pulled his short iron out of mangled rough to the side of a bunker and still had 111 yards. He hit that to 12 feet and made the par putt. He bogeyed the next from behind the green, didn't get a birdie until the par-3 eighth and then ran off consecutive birdies early on the back nine that restored his lead. He also made a 12-foot par save on the 15th hole. “Any time you’re holing those 10- to 15-footers, it’s really nice to keep the round going,” Scheffler said. “I holed a few of those today. It was definitely important to keep the momentum in the round.” The heat index topped 100 degrees, and towels soaked in ice water were available on every tee. Keith Mitchell looked utterly exhausted walking out of scoring, from the heat and from the stress of projections that keep him right at No. 49 with one round remaining. He was tied for 22nd, along with Maverick McNealy, who was projected at No. 50. Burns is thinking only about winning, and that starts with making up a two-shot deficit on the No. 1 player in the world. The only other time they've played together on a Sunday was the 2021 Tour Championship — both out of contention — though Burns did beat Scheffler with a long birdie putt in a playoff at Colonial in 2022. “Scottie is obviously playing great, as he always does. He’s not going to lay down,” Burns said. “He’s going to play great tomorrow. So you’re going to have to go out there and put a really good round together and see if you can catch him.”

Mika Salamanca reveals she once turned down Will Ashley. Fans have been following Mika Salamanca and Will Ashley’s growing closeness, but there’s one detail about their story that we didn’t know: Mika had already turned Will down before. In her latest vlog, Mika revealed that Will had tried to court her while they were filming a series. “Nung nagte-taping kami for a serye, before, si Will, nanliligaw siya sa akin,” she shared. She also remembered how Will would send fruits to her unit after picking up on the things she casually said she was craving. “Magugulat ako, galing kay Will. Lahat kami busog—lagi,” Mika recalled. Will later confirmed the surprising part of their story himself, joking, “Kung hindi mo ’ko binasted last year, e di sana araw-araw tayong ganito.” But apparently, being rejected didn't make Will give up. Mika recently opened up about where they stand now, revealing that Will has continued to make an effort. “To be honest, kung may scoring, high score kasi sobrang close namin ngayon. He has been consistent in pursuing me.” And unlike before, Mika said she's happy about his continued pursuit. Their current closeness makes the revelation even more interesting. Fans have already noticed how comfortable Mika and Will seem around each other, but knowing that Will previously courted her—and is still doing so—adds another layer to their relationship. Will first expressed his admiration for Mika during their "Pinoy Big Brother: Celebrity Collab Edition" days, and the pair later reunited as co-stars in "The Secrets of Hotel 88." So, are they officially a couple? They haven't put a label on their relationship publicly but with Mika admitting that Will is still pursuing her and that she's happy about it, fans definitely have something new to be excited about.

Gatchalian: Senate committed to transparent, accountability-driven 2027 budget. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Sunday, August 16, said the Senate is strongly committed to conducting a timely, transparent, accountability-driven process to scrutinize the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027. Despite running a busy schedule with an impeachment trial on the side, Gatchalian said the Upper Chamber is poised to hold budget hearings at the soonest possible time. “As we will soon begin committee deliberations on the proposed national budget for next year, the Senate will be guided by a strict focus on public trust, fiscal responsibility, and timely execution,” Gatchalian said. Gatchalian made the statement following the recent turnover to the Senate of the 2027 national expenditure program (NEP) by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). “Our goal is simple, and that is to ensure that every peso counts with the help of mechanisms for transparency and accountability,” he said. “Whether it is allocated for education, healthcare, infrastructure, social protection, or job creation, every peso in the 2027 budget must directly benefit the Filipino people and drive inclusive economic growth across the country,” he added. In addition to ensuring transparency and accountability in the budgeting process, Gatchalian said the Senate’s final output would include strict safeguards to that end. Earlier, Senate Finance Committee chief, Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito said the Senate will not accept any last-minute budget insertions, especially during the bicameral conference committee. Ejercito also said there would be no “secret bicams” or “small bicams” that would be held as every amendments or insertions would only be manifested during the plenary budget deliberations, which will be made public and also livestreamed. Moreover, the Senate will not allow “leadership funds” in the 2027 national budget, which former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) secretary Manuel Bonoan claimed in his testimony before the Sandiganbayan where he is facing plunder and graft cases in connection to the flood control anomalies. “As far as we are concerned, there would be no leadership fund. I will continue what Sen. (Sherwin) Gatchalian had started…” Ejercito said in an interview last Thursday.

P1-M shabu seized from drug den in Taguig. Police operatives dismantled a drug den and seized P1 million worth of shabu in Taguig on Aug. 16. The Southern Police District’s District Drug Enforcement Unit in coordination with the Taguig police conducted a buy-bust operation at about 2:40 a.m. at a residence on Village Street in Barangay Central Bicutan. During the operation, the police also arrested five suspects identified as alias Jemai, 34; alias Mohaimen, 37; alias Moonderf John, 32; alias Mark Anthony, 41; and alias Erwin, 60, who was identified as the maintainer of the drug den. Under Republic Act 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), a drug den, dive or resort is “a place where any dangerous drug and/or controlled precursor and essential chemical is administered, delivered, stored for illegal purposes, distributed, sold or used in any form.” An undercover officer acted as a poseur-buyer and negotiated a drug deal with alias Jemai, prompting back-up team members to immediately move in, secure the drug den, and apprehend all individuals present inside. The police seized five plastic sachets containing shabu weighing approximately 160 grams valued at P1.08 million, buy-bust money, and a cell phone used during the drug transaction. The suspects were brought to the DDEU-SPD office for documentation. They will face complaints for violation of Sections 5 (sale of dangerous drugs), 6 (maintenance of a drug den), 11 (possession of dangerous drugs) and 26 (conspiracy) of RA 9165 based on their levels of participation in the illegal acts. Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco, SPD district director, commended the DDEU and operating personnel for the dismantling of the drug den.

No power in parts of Tondo on Aug. 16 due to pole replacement. Parts of Tondo, Manila are scheduled to experience power interruptions on Sunday, Aug. 16, due to the replacement of electrical poles along Honorio Lopez Boulevard in Balut. Meralco issued the advisory at around 8 a.m. Sunday, with the affected areas set to experience interruptions at different times throughout the day. Portions of Circuit North Port 403H will have interruptions from 8:30 a.m. to 9 a.m. and again from 2 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The affected areas include portions of Honorio Lopez Boulevard, from near Juan Luna Street to Alcalde, Bilbao, Dalaga, Dandan and Lakandula streets, as well as a portion of Velasquez Street from Infanta Street to near Ugbo Street. A longer interruption is scheduled from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. for portions of Circuits North Port 403H and 44H. This will affect a portion of Honorio Lopez Boulevard from Infanta Street to Beltran, Buendia, C. Dayao, C. Edugue, Guidote, Kaunlaran, Nava, Pinoy, Rodriguez and Salonga streets in Balut. Meralco said the power interruption is necessary for pole replacement along Honorio Lopez Boulevard. Service may be restored earlier if the work is completed ahead of schedule.

Judy Ann Santos, RK Bagatsing and Edu Manzano as talent agents. Known for her exceptional work as actress in both TV and movies, Judy Ann Santos is among local entertainment's more respected acting talents. But can you imagine her as talent manager? Well, imagine no more. She is playing one in HBO Max's "Call My Manager." The series is based on "Dix Pour Cent," a French comedy. In an interview, Judy Ann shared with us her experience playing talent manager, describing it a whole lot of fun. "Oh, it was fun. Yeah, it was fun because this is the first time for me to actually create a character that people could love but also hate at some point." "It's a challenge because I really have to dig deep to be able to do that." While Judy Ann's character is stern, straightfoward and seemingly no nonsense, RK Bagatsing's is different in that he is too caring, panicky. "As an actor used to doing something, it was kind of like exercising a different muscle. I'm used to being the villain and Gabriel was totally different from that. He cares deeply. He's always panicking. He's always not sure about what to do. But that's the fun part. You get to depict new feelings, new emotions," RK shared. Then there's Edu Manzano who plays Matthew Buenaventura, the senior manager of their company. According to the industry veteran, the series is an exciting glimpse into the world of entertainment and the colorful characters that inhabit it. "Here we get to see how, sometimes, media and its desire to promote films, give the actors a certain color, just to make them look like they're larger than life." "And if you actually look at the lives of the managers dealing with people like us, they lead more colorful lives." Directed by Erik Matti, Mario Cornejo, and Jade Castro, ''Call My Manager" drops new episodes every Thursday.

‘Habagat’ to continue affecting Luzon, western Visayas over next 5 days — PAGASA. The southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to continue affecting Luzon and parts of Visayas over the next five days, bringing moderate to heavy rains to several areas, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Sunday, Aug. 16. PAGASA weather specialist Aldczar Aurelio said rainfall of 50 to 100 millimeters, considered as moderate to heavy, may persist over Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, and Zambales from Sunday noon to Monday noon, Aug. 17. From Monday noon to Tuesday noon, Aug. 18, moderate to heavy rains are expected over Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, and Occidental Mindoro. The rains may continue from Tuesday noon to Wednesday noon, Aug. 19, over Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Antique. Aurelio warned that localized flooding is possible, particularly in urbanized and low lying areas and those near rivers. Landslides are also possible in areas highly susceptible to the hazard. Over the next 24 hours, Metro Manila, Visayas, and the rest of Luzon will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms. The rest of the country will generally have fair weather, although isolated rain showers or thunderstorms may occur in the afternoon or evening. Meanwhile, the low-pressure area located 2,335 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility, is expected to dissipate within the next few hours. Aurelio said the LPA is not expected to affect any part of the country.

5,000 join El Shaddai anniversary rites in Manila. Around 5,000 members of El Shaddai gathered at the Quirino Grandstand in Luneta, Manila, on Saturday, Aug. 15, as the religious group began the two-day celebration of its 42nd anniversary, with more members expected to arrive for the second day on Sunday. The El Shaddai DWXI Prayer Partners Fellowship International, founded by Mike Velarde in 1984, is holding the anniversary gathering at the Quirino Grandstand on Aug. 15 and 16. The first-day gathering drew around 5,000 members to the Manila venue for prayer and anniversary activities, while organizers expect additional participants to join Sunday's events. As the celebration enters its second day on Sunday morning, members continue to gather at the grandstand, with increased pedestrian activity expected around Luneta, Quirino Grandstand and nearby roads. Authorities are also deployed around the area to assist with crowd management and public safety as participants arrive. Motorists and commuters passing through the area may encounter heavier pedestrian and vehicle activity as the anniversary gathering continues. The two-day celebration is scheduled to continue throughout Sunday, Aug. 16.

Alapag banking on familiarity with NLEX new import. NLEX head coach Jimmy Alapag is banking on his familiarity with his new import Deonte Burton as he hopes for a smooth transition for the team following the horrible injury of DeQuan Jones. Burton is set to take the place of Jones who suffered a lower leg fracture in their 118-111 win over TNT Tropang 5G last Tuesday, Aug. 11. “He'll be making his PBA debut after the break. Looking forward to having him. We spent time together in the G League and with the Kings. So, excited to have him on board,” said Alapag whose team played all-Filipino in the 112-110 loss to Converge. Alapag also had first-hand experience mentoring Burton, who played for the Stockton Kings in G-League and then later on Sacramento Kings in 2023. He played a total of 73 games in the NBA in his stints with the Kings and the Oklahoma City Thunder. More than the resume, however, Alapag is seeing Burton to be a good fit for the Road Warriors, similar to how Jones was a perfect fit to the team that led to their 7-2 record. “I think he is very comparable [to Jones.] You know, in terms of just, his explosiveness, the power, the physicality. He spent some time in the NBA and we spent time together,” said Alapag. Good thing for Burton and NLEX, they will have some time to get to know each other as the league won’t be playing games until the first week of October. “So, hopefully, hopefully, our experience working together in the past, hopefully that makes his transition to the PBA and with NLEX a little smoother than it would be with an import that hasn't played here before. So, excited to have him on board.”

Mark Rydell, Oscar-nominated director of ‘On Golden Pond,’ dies at 97. LOS ANGELES (AP) — Mark Rydell, the Oscar-nominated director of the sentimental blockbuster “On Golden Pond” who worked with such Hollywood heavyweights as Henry Fonda, Katharine Hepburn, Steve McQueen and John Wayne, has died. He was 97. His daughter, Amy Rydell, told The Hollywood Reporter that her father died Thursday of natural causes at a retirement community for the entertainment industry in the Woodland Hills section of Los Angeles. “Hard to put into words how much I loved my dad,” she posted Friday on her Instagram account. “He was truly one of a kind. Funniest and most talented person I’ve ever known.” ‘On Golden Pond’ earned 10 Oscar nominations “On Golden Pond,” which teamed Fonda with Hepburn and his daughter, Jane Fonda, was nominated for 10 Oscars. Henry Fonda and Hepburn won leading acting honors and the film won for screenplay, which Ernest Thompson adapted from his play of the same name. Rydell was nominated for directing but lost to Warren Beatty for “Reds.” It earned over $119 million at the box office, making it the second-highest grossing film of 1981 behind “Raiders of the Lost Ark.” “On Golden Pond” was Henry Fonda’s final movie role. He starred as Norman Thayer, an emotionally brittle and distant father who becomes more accessible at the end of his life after his teenage grandson spends the summer with him and his wife, Ethel (played by Hepburn), at their cottage in New England. The film’s story resembled Fonda’s real-life relationship with daughter Jane, who said working on the movie together helped resolve some of their issues. The elder Fonda died at age 77 months after winning his only Oscar. Rydell’s other Oscar-nominated films were “The Fox” in 1967, “The Reivers” with McQueen in 1969, “Cinderella Liberty” with James Caan and Marsha Mason in 1973, “The Rose” with Bette Midler in 1979, and “The River” with Mel Gibson and Sissy Spacek in 1984. Born Mortimer Harold Rydell on March 23, 1929, in New York City, he studied with jazz pianist Teddy Wilson at the Julliard School of Music. During a stint in the Army, he spent two years in Japan developing entertainment for military personnel. He majored in English and philosophy at New York University. Early acting career opposite Steiger, Cassavetes, Mineo He turned to acting when he won a scholarship to the Neighborhood Playhouse in New York. Among his early roles were on the CBS soap operas “The Edge of Night” and “As the World Turns.” Rydell made his Broadway debut in “Seagulls Over Sorrento” with Rod Steiger. In 1956, he made his movie acting debut opposite John Cassavetes and Sal Mineo in Don Siegel’s “Crime In The Streets.” Among his film acting credits were Robert Altman’s “The Long Goodbye” in 1973 and Woody Allen’s “Hollywood Ending” in 2002. Rydell moved into directing television, helming episodes of “Mr. Novak,” “Ben Casey,” “I Spy,” “The Wild Wild West,” “The Long, Hot Summer,” “The Fugitive” and “Gunsmoke.” He made his feature-film directorial debut with 1967’s “The Fox” starring Sandy Dennis, and it was a hit. Two years later, Rydell directed McQueen in the comedy-drama “The Reivers.” Teaming with Sydney Pollack Rydell and Sydney Pollack, who became friends during their acting days, formed Sanford Productions in 1971. Among their efforts were the films “Jeremiah Johnson” starring Robert Redford and “Scarecrow” with Al Pacino and Gene Hackman, which won the Cannes Film Festival’s top honor, the Palme d’Or. Rydell directed Wayne in 1972’s “The Cowboys.” He reunited with Caan for the 1976 flop “Harry and Walter Go to New York.” He scored a major hit with 1979’s “The Rose,” with Midler in her Oscar-nominated role as a self-destructive rock star loosely based on Janis Joplin. Rydell re-teamed with Caan and Midler in “For the Boys” in 1991, but it wasn’t successful. “He was an actor of note before he became a director, and I was so lucky to have met him when I did; he taught me so much on The Rose and later on For The Boys,” Midler posted on Instagram. “Two Oscars nominations both because of him. He was the actor’s whisperer; just a few words was all it took to understand what was needed. Devoted to Meisner. So many happy memories.” TV movies and series among his credits Rydell directed the pilot of the hit ABC drama “Family” in 1976. Among his TV movie directing credits were “McBride and Groom,” “Crime of the Century” with Isabella Rossellini and Stephen Rea, and “James Dean,” which earned actor James Franco a Golden Globe award. Rydell also appeared in the movie as Warner Bros. chief Jack Warner. He directed the movies “Intersection” in 1994 and “Even Money” in 2006. In 2009, Rydell, Oscar-winning actor Martin Landau and screenwriter Lyle Kessler taught a film workshop at UCLA. Rydell and Landau were co-artistic directors of The Actors Studio West, teaching and coaching actors, writers and directors. “All great art rests on telling the truth,” Rydell told UCLA’s student newspaper The Daily Bruin. “The real pursuit of an artist is to tell the truth.” Besides his daughter, he is survived by son Christopher. The siblings who went into acting were from his first marriage to actor Joanne Linville. He had another son, Alexander, from his second marriage to producer Esther Rydell.

Drinking sessions turn violent: 1 stabbed dead, another shot after being noisy in Rizal. Two separate drinking sessions in Rizal province turned violent after stabbing and shooting incidents left one man dead and another wounded on Saturday, Aug. 15. In Barangay Cuyambay, Tanay, Rizal, a man identified as “Edwin” died after his drinking buddy, “Marlon,” allegedly stabbed him at around 11:30 p.m. The Tanay Municipal Police Station said the stabbing stemmed from a heated argument between the suspect and the victim, with the reason still under investigation. Authorities said the argument escalated into a physical altercation, during which the suspect allegedly stabbed the victim with an unidentified bladed weapon. The suspect fled in an unknown direction, allegedly carrying the weapon used in the commission of the crime. The victim was immediately brought to the Army Station Hospital in Sampaloc, Tanay, Rizal, for medical attention but was declared dead on arrival. “The exact number and nature of the injuries sustained by the victim are still subject to the findings of the autopsy examination,” police said. Noisy drinking buddy Meanwhile, a shooting incident also occurred during a drinking session in Baras around 12 a.m. on Sunday, Aug. 16, leaving a man injured. Based on the investigation, “Ricky,” the suspect, “Christian,” the victim, and a witness were drinking together in Barangay Rizal when an argument ensued after the victim allegedly became noisy. During the argument, the suspect allegedly drew a firearm from his sling bag and cocked it, which accidentally discharged and hit the ground. He then cocked the firearm again, which discharged and hit the victim in the right leg/thigh. The suspect fled the scene, while the victim was immediately brought to Amang Hospital for treatment. Authorities said both suspects in the two incidents remain at large and are being pursued.

Legarda pushes for lower call, text rates and non-expiring load. Senator Loren Legarda is now pushing for a bill seeking to bring down the default cost of prepaid calls and text messages to more reasonable levels reflective of modern telecommunications technology, network capacity and consumer usage. Legarda, in filing Senate Bill No. 2402, or the proposed SULIT Load Act, said it is imperative to strengthen protections against unexpected load deductions, unclear promo pricing, and the loss of prepaid value already paid for by subscribers. The senator noted that while telecommunications technology has advanced considerably and promos have made calls, texts, and mobile data much cheaper, many default or out-of-promo rates remain disproportionately expensive for ordinary prepaid users. “Telecommunications technology has changed tremendously. Networks are faster, the volume of calls, texts, and data is much higher, and there is an abundance of affordable promos,” Legarda said. “It is therefore reasonable to ask: why do standard rates for texts and calls seem stuck in the past? It is time to align pricing with today’s technology and reality,” she pointed out. Under SB No. 2402, the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), together with the DICT, DTI, and Philippine Competition Commission (PCC), would be mandated to review and rationalize regular prepaid rates for SMS, mobile calls, data, and mobile-to-landline calls based on actual costs, competition, prevailing promo rates, consumer usage, and regional pricing. Pending the completion of that review, the bill proposes interim maximum default rates of ₱0.50 per SMS, ₱2.00 per minute for ordinary domestic mobile calls, and ₱3.00 per minute for mobile-to-landline calls. The senator said the reform is long overdue because regular load should not function as an expensive fallback whenever a subscriber forgets to register for a promo, exhausts an allocation, loses internet access, or needs to make an urgent call. “If it is possible to offer very affordable calls, texts, and data through various promos, there should also be reasonable pricing for standard usage. A subscriber shouldn't be penalized simply because their promo has expired or they need to make an urgent call,” she said. The bill also seeks clearer pricing of prepaid promos as it mandates telecommunications providers to disclose, where applicable, the effective cost per gigabyte of data, call minute, SMS, and landline call minute, together with the promo's total price, validity period, restrictions, and treatment of unused allocations. Consumers should not have to navigate complicated promo names and inclusions simply to determine which offer provides better value, the lawmaker insisted. “When we buy rice, gasoline, or other products, there are prices and measurements that can be compared. It should be the same for mobile load. It should be easy to see the actual cost per GB, per minute of calls, or per text,” she said. “The subscriber has already paid for that load. As long as the account is active, there is no valid reason for the money used to purchase it to simply disappear,” Legarda said. The proposed law also seeks to address the high cost of calling landlines and essential service numbers, particularly those used by banks, hospitals, schools, utilities, airlines, government offices, and customer service centers. Legarda noted that prepaid subscribers can lose substantial load simply while waiting on hold before receiving actual assistance. “Waiting shouldn't come at a high price. When a prepaid subscriber is placed on hold—whether at a hospital, a bank, or a government hotline—their load balance continues to be deducted even though they have yet to receive the actual service. That is precisely one of the issues this proposal seeks to address,” she stressed. Moreover, under the bill, government offices providing frontline and public-facing services would also be required to establish at least one mobile-accessible contact channel, so citizens are not forced to rely solely on landline numbers that may be costly to call from prepaid mobile phones. “Mobile phones have become the primary means of communication for so many Filipinos. Public service must keep pace with this. A person should not have to spend a large amount of money just to follow up on documents, benefits, complaints, or government services,” Legarda said. “This kind of protection is long overdue. The telecommunications industry has advanced rapidly, and consumers should feel the benefits of that progress—in terms of pricing, transparency, and how the prepaid load they paid for is handled,” she stressed.

DBM settles P9.8-billion debt to 108 state colleges for free tuition. The government released ₱9.75 billion to address long-standing funding shortfalls under its tuition-free tertiary education program, clearing obligations that forced state colleges and universities to absorb costs for three academic years. In a statement on Sunday, Aug. 16, Acting Budget Secretary Kim Robert C. de Leon, said they funneled the funds through the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) to cover arrears at 108 state universities and colleges spanning the 2022 to 2025 academic years. The disbursement will be drawn from the 2026 national budget and the Higher Education Development Fund. De Leon said the release aims to ease financial strain on state institutions, which were forced to dip into internal operational funds to sustain free tuition and subsidize student fees mandated under the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act. The law, signed in 2017, guarantees free tuition and school fees in public higher education institutions nationwide. “Every peso in the national budget has competing demands,” De Leon said. “With this release, we are making nearly 10 billion pesos available to address funding requirements of our state universities and colleges while maintaining that careful fiscal balance.” The cash injection gives universities fiscal room to redirect institutional resources toward deferred capital expenditures and campus operations. Beyond settling back pay, De Leon said the funds are expected to support laboratory and library upgrades, IT infrastructure, facility maintenance, and expanding campus infrastructure. Sustaining access to higher education remains a central pillar of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s human capital agenda, even as his economic team balances social spending against tight fiscal constraints. The Marcos administration is working to narrow its budget deficit while managing rising public debt levels. “Government resources are not unlimited,” De Leon said. “Our responsibility is to make sure that limited government resources are directed where they are most needed, without compromising other equally important programs and services.: The budget department said that funding will be systematically disbursed via the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education once compliance and verification guidelines are finalized.

Meralco targets lower power bills with new push against electricity theft. Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) is ramping up infrastructure investments and cracking down on illegal connections as part of its multi-pronged strategy to drive down system losses that drive up consumer electricity bills. In a statement on Sunday, Aug. 16, Larry Fernandez, Meralco head of utility economics, said the country’s largest power distributor is balancing physical grid upgrades with stricter anti-theft operations to target both technical and non-technical inefficiencies across its distribution network. To curb technical losses—the energy naturally dissipated as heat through lines and transformers—Meralco is expanding substation capacity and upgrading distribution lines to optimize overall network efficiency. On the non-technical side, which primarily stems from unauthorized hookups and power theft, Meralco is pairing aggressive enforcement actions with redesigned infrastructure built to physically deter tampering. System loss charges passed along to end-users remain a contentious component of monthly electric bills in the country. Fernandez noted that recovering a portion of these costs from consumers is explicitly permitted under Republic Act No. 7832, known as the Anti-Electricity and Electric Transmission Lines/Materials Pilferage Act, as well as the landmark Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001. However, Meralco said that revenue recovered from penalizing power thieves does not stay on its balance sheet. Instead, all financial settlements collected from apprehended violators are returned directly to legitimate customers in the form of bill deductions. Looking ahead, Meralco plans to accelerate the deployment of smart grids and advanced metering infrastructure across its franchise area. The modern distribution systems will allow real-time monitoring of power flow, enabling the utility to pinpoint technical disruptions instantly, identify abnormal usage patterns linked to theft, and balance energy loads more efficiently for residential and commercial customers.

June Mar Fajardo delays Gilas retirement as Cone rues manpower woes. June Mar Fajardo is set to hang up his Gilas Pilipinas jersey already but had to postpone that as head coach Tim Cone continues to deal with manpower issues ahead of the August window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers. The Nationals will be missing the services of Mike Phillips and Quentin Millora-Brown at the frontline while Kai Sotto’s availability remains uncertain, leaving the veteran coach with only AJ Edu as his only legitimate center on the roster. And the depleted ceiling comes at a time when Gilas is in dire need of victory against Jordan and Iran to stay in the hunt for the World Cup spot. “QMB is doubtful with his back surgery. Mike Phillips has his brother's wedding, so he's begging off. We had June Mar wanting to retire, but we pulled him back in,” revealed Cone. Fajardo, now already 36 years old, has been part of the national team since 2013 and is actually already entertaining the idea of retiring with towering younger big men joining the team. But according to Cone, the Nationals have no other choice but call him back in. “We certainly have our issues. It's really on me to make sure we get all the best players. We haven't been able to do that. I've been failing at my job,” admitted Cone. Aside from Fajardo, expected to hold the fort for Gilas are the remaining players in the lineup in the likes of Kevin Quiambao, Carl Tamayo, Juan Gomez de Liaño, Scottie Thompson and RJ Abarrientos. Also expected to step up are Edu, Troy Rosario, Chris Newsome, Dwight Ramos and naturalized player Justin Brownlee. “I just haven't been able to get all the best players. But we've still got Dwight and Carl and KQ and Justin. So we're going to put up a fight here. We have AJ Edu still playing for us,” said Cone. “We lack a little bit more size, but it is what it is.”

More localities under state of calamity due to ‘habagat,’ cyclones; death toll increases to 23. The number of areas placed under a state of calamity has risen to 50 as the impact of the combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) and tropical cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay” became more apparent, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) disclosed Sunday, Aug. 16. Based on the latest disaster monitoring data of the OCD, Central Luzon (Region 3) and Calabarzon (Region 4A) have 24 areas each under a state of calamity while Ilocos (Region 2) has two areas under the same status. The areas declared under a state of calamity in Central Luzon were Pampanga, with all 21 cities and municipalities under a province-wide state of calamity due to flooding and damage; and Calumpit, Hagonoy, and Bulakan in Bulacan province. In Calabarzon, the entire province of Cavite covering 23 cities and municipalities were under a state of calamity, as well as Montalban town in Rizal province. In Ilocos Region, the two areas under a state of calamity were Dagupan City and Santa Barbara town, both in Pangasinan. The death toll also climbed to 23, with Benguet accounting for 15 deaths, Rizal and Batangas with three fatalities apiece, and one each in La Union and Quezon Province. The disaster has also left 17 people injured and three missing individuals. The widespread impact of the weather disturbance has now affected 1,410,800 families or 4,903,086 individuals across Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), Central Luzon (Region 3), National Capital Region (NCR), Calabarzon (Region 4A), Mimaropa (Region 4B), Bicol (Region 5), Western Visayas (Region 6), and Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9). Of this, there were 9,101 families or 31,456 individuals temporarily sheltering in 407 evacuation centers. The latest assessment also recorded damage to 1,845 houses, of which, 1,667 were partially damaged while 178 were totally destroyed. Infrastructure losses have reached P3.360 billion while damage to agriculture was estimated at P689.66 million, making the losses to more than P4.05 billion. The government has so far provided P654.59 million worth of assistance to affected communities.

CHED calls for stronger regional cooperation on AI in higher education. The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) is pushing stronger regional cooperation to advance the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI), expand academic partnerships, and promote innovation-driven, future-ready learning across the Asia-Pacific. CHED Executive Director Atty. Cinderella Filipina Benitez-Jaro made the call during the Sixth China-ASEAN Education Research Network Meeting in Guiyang, China, where she emphasized the role of AI in transforming higher education and preparing graduates for an increasingly digital and interconnected world. “Artificial intelligence is no longer confined to a single discipline. It is transforming teaching and learning, research, quality assurance, institutional governance, and innovation across higher education. As such, AI must be harnessed responsibly to enhance educational quality, inclusivity, and resilience,” Benitez-Jaro said. She highlighted CHED’s continuing initiatives to strengthen digital transformation in Philippine higher education through policies and international partnerships that promote innovation, research collaboration, academic mobility, and capacity-building. Benitez-Jaro also cited the importance of regional platforms such as the China-ASEAN Education Cooperation Week (CAECW) in facilitating policy dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaborative solutions to shared educational challenges. These efforts form part of CHED’s ACHIEVE Agenda, the Commission’s seven-point reform framework for higher education, and support President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s priority of strengthening the country’s human capital by preparing Filipinos with the skills needed for a fast-changing, technology-driven economy. “As we gather for the CAECW and the Sixth Asia-Pacific Education Research Network, let us reaffirm a shared responsibility to ensure that AI serves humanity, education must remain a force for peace and sustainable development, and our partnerships build a higher education community that is innovative, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of our peoples,” she said. Meanwhile, Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz highlighted the long-term value of educational exchanges in strengthening Philippines-China bilateral relations. “Such educational exchanges greatly contribute to fostering a deeper understanding of the cultures of the Philippines and China and strengthening people-to-people ties that promote a more harmonious diplomatic relations between the two nations,” FlorCruz said.

House to start 2027 budget deliberations; sets sights on 2 goals. The House of Representatives is out to accomplish two things as it begins to tackle the P7.2-trillion 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) or proposed national budget on Monday, Aug. 17. One, to approve next year's spending plan in a timely and transparent manner; and second, to do so while performing its task as prosecutor in Vice President Sara Duterte's ongoing Senate impeachment trial. The NEP deliberations will begin Monday with a briefing by the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) on the sources of financing, expenditure levels and the budget proposals of departments, agencies and government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs). The DBCC is composed of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM); Department of Economy, Planning and Development (DEPDev); Department of Finance (DOF); and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). Monday will also be day 16 of Vice President Duterte's impeachment trial, wherein prosecutors aim to convict the respondent and remove her from office, as well as have her perpetually disqualified from seeking an elective post. It was the House of Representatives, through the Committee on Justice chaired by Batangas 2nd district Rep. Gerville "Jinky Bitrics" Luistro, that prepared the four articles of impeachment against Duterte based on the four impeachment impeachment complaints filed against her this year. Over at the Committee on Appropriations, its chairperson, Nueva Ecija 1st district Rep. Mikaela Angela "Mika" Suansing planned a quick turnaround for the start of the NEP discussions. It was only last Aug. 11 when DBM Acting Secretary Kim Robert de Leon submitted the budget proposal to the House of Representatives . The outlay was presented to House officials led by Speaker Isabela 6th district Rep. Faustino "Bojie" Dy III and Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos. On Tuesday, Aug, 18, the appropriations panel will be briefed by the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR). According to the DBM, the agencies and sectors with the largest allocations in the proposed 2027 budget are the following: Department of Education (DepEd), P976 billion; Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), P644 billion ( including over P100 billion for flood control ); Health Sector, P353.8 billion (Department of Health [DOH] and PhilHealth combined); Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), P332.5 billion; Department of National Defense (DND), P328.8 billion; Transport Sector, P302.2 billion; Agriculture Sector: P261.7 billion, Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), P241.6 billion; State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), P176.5 billion; and Judiciary, P86.3 billion. Former deputy speaker, Manila 6th district Rep. Bienvenido "Benny" Abante Jr. underscored that the House leadership has committed to make the budget process transparent. “Wala dapat sekreto sa budget. Kailangan malaman ng taong bayan lahat ng bagay na yan,” he said. (There should be no secrets in the budget. The people need to know everything about it.) “Nagpapalamat ako sa leadership ng House of Representatives na ginagawa naming transparent ang deliberations. Kailangang malaman ng taong bayan kung saan napupunta 'yung budget ng gobyerno sapagkat 'yan ay pera ng mga nagbabayad ng buwis,” he added. (I thank the leadership of the House of Representatives for making our deliberations transparent. The people must know where the government’s budget goes because that is the money of the taxpayers.) VP Duterte trial won't derail NEP deliberations Abante expressed confidence that the conduct of the impeachment trial won't derail the House’s deliberations on the 2027 NEP--the largest in history. “Palagay ko hindi naman [maaapektuhan] sapagkat nakita naman natin… four hours lang naman ang impeachment court. Sa umaga nagsisimula, three o’clock deliberation na ‘yan eh, so I don’t think maapektuhan,” Abante said. (I don’t think [it will be affected], because as we’ve seen, the impeachment court only runs for four hours. It starts in the morning and by three o’clock deliberations are already happening, so I don’t think it will be affected),” Abante said. Impeachment hearings only take place from Monday to Wednesday. Suansing earlier bared a 53-day timetable for the passage of the eventual House General Appropriations Bill (GAB) on third and final reading . Abante said that if the Senate and the House pass different versions of the 2027 GAB, a Bicameral Conference Committee will be convened to reconcile the versions. “After that it will go to the President for his signature. Kapag 'yan ay pinirmahan ng Pangulo, 'yan ay magiging General Appropriations Act or law (Once it is signed by the President, it becomes the GAA or law). That would become the national budget,” he noted. True transparency needed Meanwhile, deputy minority leader ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio called for "true transparency" in the 2027 budget process, even as he slammed last year's livestreaming of the bicam hearings as "perfomative". "We need true transparency in the budget process, not the same spectacle that the President himself announced last year," Tinio said on Sunday, Aug. 16. The Makabayan lawmaker pointed out that the unprecedented livestreaming of the bicam deliberations for the 2026 budget in December last year was undertaken after it was exposed that funds inserted at the bicam level funded questionable items, including anomalous flood control projects. "That livestream was nothing but damage control. Pakitang-tao lang (it was just for show). Yet, it was the President himself who made the announcement," Tinio added. "The Marcos administration cannot hide behind performative transparency while perpetuating the same corrupt budgetary practices that have robbed the people of genuine public services and development. True transparency demands the dismantling of all pork barrel mechanisms, not just cameras in the bicam," he concluded.

Eala to face world No. 10 Anisimova in Cincinnati third round. Another elite player awaits Alex Eala on court when she faces world No. 10 Amanda Anisimova in the third round of the Cincinnati Open in Ohio on Monday, Aug. 17. This would be the first time that the 21-year-old Eala is competing against the two-time Grand Slam finalist, who ranked as high as No. 3 early this year. Eala, seeded 17th, is coming off a dominant 6-1, 3-0 (ret) second round win over Elena-Gabriela Ruse, who retired with a right foot injury. “It’s unfortunate that we weren’t able to continue the match and first and foremost, just wish Gabby a speedy recovery. Health is just the number one priority for everybody so I hope she gets better soon,” the Filipina said in a post-match interview. “I think I played really well. I think I found my groove and I was able to hold that until I guess the end of the match, so I’m really happy with it,” she added. The 24-year-old Anisimova, meanwhile, is fresh from a 6-2, 6-3 thumping of Zeynep Sonmez. Seeded ninth in this WTA 1000 tournament, the American star said she is thrilled to face Eala for the first time. “I haven’t played her (Eala) before. She’s been having such an incredible season, incredible year. Very great player with a lot of tennis fans,” Anisimova said. She also expected a big crowd in their match, knowing how Eala’s fan base has grown over the past months. “I’m really looking forward to that. I know that it’s probably gonna be a very packed stadium. I’m sure it will be really fun,” she said. While Eala has an impressive two-week stretch that saw her winning her breakthrough WTA Tour title at the Mubadala DC Open and a fourth-round finish at the National Bank Open in Toronto, Anisimova, for her part has an impressive run at the Grand Slams that include a quarterfinal finish at the Australian Open and third-round finished at the French Open and the Wimbledon. Another win over Anisimova would give Eala her seventh victory against a Top 10 player this season and her 10th overall in her career. It would also set up a next match with the winner between reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and Clara Tauson.

AFP vows to hunt down attackers of Macacua’s convoy; steps up BARMM security. The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) vowed on Sunday, Aug. 16, to pursue those behind the attack on the convoy of BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua in Maguindanao del Norte as it intensified security operations in vulnerable areas across the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) to protect the upcoming parliamentary elections. General Antonio Nafarrete, AFP chief of staff, condemned the strafing of Macacua’s convoy in Barangay Bitu, Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte on Aug. 15 although the incident did not cause physical harm to the BARMM chief minister. “The AFP will pursue the perpetrators and work closely with the Philippine National Police, Commission on Elections, and other concerned agencies to identify those responsible and ensure that they are held accountable under the law,” Nafarrete said. Security forces have since intensified their presence along major routes and other areas considered vulnerable to attacks. Authorities have yet to identify the gunmen behind the strafing. The attack came as BARMM prepares for its inaugural parliamentary elections on September 14, a major step in the political transition under the Bangsamoro peace process. Nafarrete urged the public to remain calm and avoid actions that could further raise tensions in the region. “The AFP calls on political leaders, candidates, communities, and the Bangsamoro people to remain calm, exercise restraint, and work together to ensure a peaceful, safe, and credible electoral environment,” he said. “We remain committed to protecting the people, preserving peace and order, and supporting the peaceful conduct of the BARMM elections so that the people of Bangsamoro can exercise their right to vote freely and without fear, contributing to a peaceful and stable BARMM,” he added. Army is undeterred in securing BARMM Meanwhile, the Philippine Army (PA) said the incident would not weaken its commitment to securing the elections. “While the Chief Minister was unharmed following the attack, this incident does not change our resolve,” Lt. Gen. Donald M. Gumiran, Army commanding general, said. Gumiran said a credible election would be an important step for the Bangsamoro government and the Army, he added, would help ensure that voters could choose their leaders without fear. “A credible and transparent election this September will be a huge step forward for the Bangsamoro regional government and the Philippine Army is committed to helping ensure that the Bangsamoro voters can exercise the right to elect their next leaders,” he said. The Army said its units had intensified security operations at known vulnerable points, including major highways and transit routes across the region. “The Philippine Army assures the Bangsamoro people that we remain steadfast in our commitment to protect communities, preserve peace and order, and support a safe and credible electoral environment,” Gumiran said. Last week, the Army deployed 561 soldiers under Task Force 92 to Maguindanao to help secure the first BARMM parliamentary elections, protect voters, and prevent threats and intimidation. The task force, organized by the 1st Brigade Combat Team, was sent off at Fort Magsaysay on Aug. 5 and will initially operate under the 602nd Infantry Brigade in parts of Maguindanao, the Bangsamoro Special Geographic Area, and North Cotabato. Led by Lt. Col. Anacito C. Naz, Task Force 92 includes infantry, intelligence, mortar, EOD, K9, civil-military operations, combat engineer and sustainment units. It will also conduct community engagement and coordinate with government agencies. The deployment added to at least 1,500 additional Army troops already mobilized in BARMM to strengthen security and enforce the election gun ban.

Cone still hoping for Boatwright stint in Asian Games. Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone is still hoping that Bennie Boatwright could somehow be available for the national team’s title defense in the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games next month. Cone, himself, initially ruled out Boatwright for the tournament last week, noting that the Asian Games Organizing Committee had already stricken the 6-foot-10 center out of the list but the veteran coach revealed he hasn’t really given up on having the former San Miguel import for the team. “We were hoping that Benny would be alright to play in the Asian Games (but) that looks very doubtful at this point,” said Cone. The Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas, however, is closely monitoring the developments on Boatwright's naturalization papers which are only needing a signature from President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. The naturalization bill could also lapse into a law after 30 days since being forwarded to Malacañang which would allow Boatwright to process his Philippine passport. Should Boatwright, somehow, make it, it would be a big boost for the Nationals who are keen to field an all-PBA players team along with naturalized player Justin Brownlee. However, it also remains to be seen if Brownlee is back to his top shape after struggling in the last window of the FIBA World Cup qualifiers due to injuries. At this point, there is no plan of bringing Boatwright back in the country unless given the green light to play for the Asian Games.

Attempt on BARMM leader's life 'especially alarming', says Adiong. House Assistant Majority Leader Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong has described as "especially alarming" the attack on the convoy of Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua. "We strongly condemn the brazen attempt on the life of BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua. We demand justice through a swift, thorough, and complete investigation of this reprehensible crime," Adiong said in a statement Sunday, Aug. 16, a day after the attack. Adiong says the attack strikes not only at the Chief Minister but at the very foundation of the Bangsamoro peace process. "It is especially alarming that this violence has occurred barely one month before the historic Sept. 14, 2026 BARMM Parliamentary Elections—the region’s first regular parliamentary elections—when the Bangsamoro people are preparing to exercise their democratic will," he noted. "We cannot and will not allow violence, intimidation, or fear to undermine what generations have struggled and sacrificed to achieve," stressed the solon from Mindanao. As such, Adiong called on the country's law enforcement agencies to go after Macacua's attackers. "Those responsible must be identified, apprehended, and brought to justice without delay. The Bangsamoro people deserve nothing less than the full truth and unwavering accountability." He also told his fellow Mindanaoans that dialogue remains an option for resolving conflict. "We therefore call on all parties to resolve every grievance through dialogue, democratic institutions, and the rule of law—not through the barrel of a gun," Adiong said. "Let justice be swift and complete. And let nothing derail the Bangsamoro people’s historic journey toward lasting peace and genuine self-governance," he further said.

Galdiano trails leader by 6 in Portland Classic. Mariel Galdiano continued to slip on the leaderboard of The Standard Portland Classic after carding a 2-under-par 70 for a share of 16th place after three rounds on Sunday, Aug. 16 (Philippine time). Galdiano, a Hawaiian of Filipino parentage, fired four birdies against two bogeys on the front nine to post a three-round total of 206, six strokes off co-leaders Sophia Schubert and Aripchaya Yubol. Schubert joined Yubol at the helm after posting a 67 for 200, while Yubol stayed on top with a 68. Galdiano started hot by leading the opening round with a 65, before losing steam with a 71 to trail second-round leader Yubol by four strokes. The leaders are winless on the LPGA Tour, with the 30-year-old Schubert back on the big tour after finishing 10th in the Epson Tour standings last year. The American — the 2017 U.S. Women’s Amateur winner — is ranked 295th in the world and is 125th in the tour’s points race. “I love the Epson Tour. It’s great. I loved playing out there,” Schubert said. “I think it was a great boost for my confidence. Competition is great and you get the sense of winning.” The 24-year-old Yubol, from Thailand, is ranked 112th in the world and is 28th in the tour's season standings. She finished second this year at Mayakoba and the ShopRite LPGA. “I try to be relaxed because like be leader group and also the leader score, you cannot stay on your score,” Yubol said. “You have to be moving up.” Fellow Thai player Jeeno Thitikul was third, two strokes back after a 67, to take final spot in the last group Sunday. She’s chasing her 10th LPGA Tour victory. “We’re playing golf because we love to be in contention,” Thitikul said. “We love to chasing the trophy.” Narin An shot 66 to get to 13 under.

Marcos condemns attack on BARMM chief minister. President Marcos has condemned the armed attack at the convoy of Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua in Maguindanao del Norte. The President, according to Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro, ordered all government agencies to tighten the security in Bangsamoro communities and conduct thorough investigation to identify those behind the shooting incident. He also assured them that the incident will not weaken the government's commitment to helping BARMM carry out a smooth transition to a democratic governance. "Ang naganap na karahasan na ginawa kina BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua at mga kasamahan niya ay kinokondena ng Pangulo (The President condemns the violence carried out against BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua and his companions)," Castro said on Sunday, Aug. 16. "Ngunit sinisiguro naman na hindi ito magpapahina sa naisin ng gobyerno para sa BARMM communities na magkaroon ng maayos na paglipat o pagbabago patungo sa pamamahalang demokratiko (However, he assures the public that this incident will not weaken the government’s commitment to helping the BARMM communities achieve a smooth transition toward democratic governance)," Castro added. Marcos also called on the public to remain calm and uphold humanity. "Nananawagan si Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. na maging mahinahon at pairalin ang pagiging makatao na may respeto sa karapatan lalong lalo sa buhay ng bawat kababayan natin (President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is calling on everyone to remain calm and uphold humanity and respect for the rights of every Filipino, especially the right to life)," Castro said. According to authorities, the attack took place along the National Highway in Barangay Bitu, Datu Odin Sinsuat at around 4:44 p.m. on Aug. 15. Initial information showed that the attackers fled in an unknown direction after the incident while the convoy proceeded toward Cotabato City.

Baguio distributes P3.1-M assistance during calamity. BAGUIO CITY – The City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) here reported that an initial P3.1 million worth of assistance were given to disaster victims in the city following the devastation caused by Typhoon Maymay and the strengthened southwest monsoon that brought heavy rains the past two weeks. According to CSWD Officer Liza Bulayungan, the assistance consisted of food, non-food, and cash assistance from the local government, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and donations from individuals and organizations. The assistance from the local government included food packs, hygiene kits, emergency shelter assistance, and financial assistance. The DSWD-CAR also delivered assistance consisting of food packs, hygiene kits, family kits, kitchen kits, sleeping kits, and financial assistance. Bulayungan said there were also about P2.1 million worth of donations from individuals and civic-minded groups, consisting of food, non-food items, and cash, given to the affected victims. Based on the data, there was a total of 243 families, consisting of 1,112 individuals, which were affected by the weather disturbances that hit the city in the past two weeks. Of these, 125 families or 530 people had to leave their homes. For the population of those displaced, there were 33 families consisting of 132 individuals who were inside evacuation centers at the time of reporting. Bulayungan said there were about 47 houses reported to have been damaged by the weather changes, of which 41 structures were partially damaged and six houses were completely destroyed.

North banks on pressure game as South eyes home-course equalizer. CAGAYAN DE ORO – Team North will open its title defense in the ICTSI Elite Junior PGT Finals with a simple formula: play clean, stay patient and keep the pressure on until host South cracks. But with South armed with home-course familiarity, a deeper pool of battle-tested qualifiers and a determined bid to avenge last year’s defeat, North knows it cannot afford to take anything for granted when the Ryder Cup-style championship gets under way Tuesday, Aug. 18, at Pueblo de Oro Golf and Country Club. Coach Joey Anciano has stressed teamwork and smart decision-making as the keys to North’s campaign, particularly in the opening four-ball and foursomes matches where partnerships and momentum can quickly swing the complexion of the competition. “Our main focus is teamwork and keeping the pressure on. In both formats, we want our players to play smart, stay patient, and trust their partners,” said Anciano. “But the goal is to play clean golf and let them make the mistakes,” he added. That approach will be tested immediately as North faces a South side determined to turn its local knowledge into an early lead. The Southerners are expected to draw confidence from their familiarity with Pueblo de Oro, particularly in the delicate shots around the greens, while several new faces have strengthened the lineup after earning places through the grueling six-leg regional qualifying series. South also believes that knowing the course can provide the kind of small but potentially decisive edge that matters in match play – where a good read on a breaking putt, knowledge of a difficult landing area or confidence on a particular approach can turn a halved hole into a lost point for the opposition. North, however, has already shown it can thrive under pressure. The defending champions stormed to a commanding 26 1/2-21 1/2 victory over South in last year’s inaugural showdown at The Country Club, and Anciano’s charges are confident they have enough depth and firepower to reproduce that performance – or improve on it – even on what figures to be hostile turf. With points at a premium across all age groups, including the 7-10, 11-14 and 15-18 categories, North knows that depth could prove just as important as star power. Anciano has kept his final pairings under wraps, emphasizing that the strength of his roster gives him plenty of options before the opening tee shots. “The great thing about this team is that every single player is strong, so no matter how we order our pairs, we’re confident we can win points from the very first match to the last,” Anciano said. “We’ll save the final order for game day.” That flexibility could prove crucial in a competition where momentum often carries from one match to the next.

Family's harrowing trip through pothole littered highway in Rosario, La Union. LA UNION -- A family’s trip turned into hours of agony and distress as they had to negotiate deep, water-filled potholes along the national highway in Nagtagaan, Rosario, La Union, that also resulted into damaging three tires of their vehicle. Danica Guevara said in her Facebook post that they first hit a large pothole before dark, damaging one tire. Later, while driving slowly at night, they hit another pothole that was difficult to see because it was filled with rainwater. Two more tires, including the newly installed spare, were damaged. Another vehicle reportedly hit the same pothole less than an hour later, damaging two tires. The motorists are now appealing to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) La Union, DPWH Region 1, and the Municipal Government of Rosario to inspect the area and install warning signs, reflectors, or barricades while permanent repairs are pending. "Talagang kakabahan ka sa pagbiyahe kapag gabi maliban sa malakas na ulan na minsan zero visibility pa tapos may hindi ka inaasahan na malaking butas sa kalsada maiiyak ka na lang sa trauma," a motorist who travel a lot from Pangasinan to La Union said. For motorists, the concern goes beyond damaged tires and expenses—it is about preventing the next road accident . "Nandiyan lamang sa La Union ang Regional Office kaya dapat mas mabilis na aksiyon," another motorist told the Manila Bulletin.

Fish released into Burnham Lake as part of rehab efforts. BAGUIO CITY – Fish stocking has begun at the rehabilitated Burnham Lake as part of efforts to improve not only the area but also the recreational activities it can provide to residents and visitors. The first fish stocking was conducted by fishing enthusiasts Rafael Serrano and Michael Rosero after Mayor Benjamin Magalong and the City Environment and Parks Management Office (CEPMO), under Atty. Rhenan Diwas, approved the experiment. Five tilapia fingerlings were placed in the lake to determine whether the fish could survive under its current conditions. The fish will be monitored for three days. If the trial is successful, about 1,000 fish will be introduced into the lake. The fish are expected to be ready for fishing within three months. The initiative is also preparing for a planned fishing tournament in the lake in December. Rosero said he is willing to provide tilapia for the trial phase if the newly rehabilitated lake proves viable. Serrano is behind a series of fishing tournaments held at the lake in partnership with the city government. The activity is part of an ongoing effort to rehabilitate and improve Burnham Park Lake for the public, with the park set to open on September 1.

FBI most wanted living in Iloilo - family. ILOILO CITY—A man wanted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in the United States (US) for a $650-million investment scam has been living in Iloilo since 2022. The family of Rey E. Grabato II, the son of Mina town mayor Rey Grabato, II once again reiterated his presence in Iloilo after the FBI identified Rey II as a Most Wanted Fraudster with a reward of $150,000 for his arrest. Rey II’s younger brother Christopher issued an August 14 statement on behalf of the family claiming that Rey II “is presently recovering from a severe stroke, which caused him to be partially paralyzed. The family urged for restraint and sensitivity. It was Rey II’s mother, former mayor Linda Grabato, who initially announced last October 2022 that Rey II came home to Iloilo months prior to recover from an accident in the US. At that time, Rey II was indicted after being charged by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for defrauding thousands of investors via the National Realty Investment Advisors LLC (NRIA), wherein he served as president. Rey II’s presence in Iloilo is still being confirmed by the Manila Bulletin. But photos taken in 2023 showed Rey II in various social and business engagements with individuals who were unaware he had been a wanted fugitive in the US. It was unclear when Rey II had a stroke, but the photos taken of him in 2023 showed him apparently being able to have physical mobility. The family also emphasized that Rey II or the family never received any official notice from authorities in the Philippines and the US. “We consider it inappropriate at this time to speculate on, debate, or publicly litigate the substance of the allegations appearing in media and social media reports,” Christopher wrote. “Any appropriate response concerning the legal matters being reported will be made through the proper channels should and when formal proceedings require it,” the statement added. Aside from the investment scam, Rey II was also accused of “conspiring to evade $26 million in tax liabilities” with the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

'Buti naman': Libanan sees lower electricity rates, refunds for Visayas consumers over flawed charges. House Minority Leader 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino “Nonoy” Libanan happily shared that Visayas consumers are expected to benefit from lower electricity rates following the Energy Regulatory Commission's (ERC) suspension on the flawed collection of excessive Line Loss and Congestion Cost (LLCC) charges. “We expect to see lower power rates in the Visayas, and refunds to consumers who saw their electricity bills surge by anywhere from P2.00 to P5.99 per kilowatt-hour because of the erroneous pass-on of excessive LLCC charges,” Libanan said on Sunday, Aug. 16. Prior to the ERC decision, Libanan had lashed out at the exorbitant LLCC charges during the Aug. 11 hearing of the House Committee on Energy, which was attended by officials from the ERC and the Department of Energy (DOE). The lawmaker’s intervention came after the Eastern Samar Electric Cooperative Inc. (ESAMELCO) sought his assistance over what it described as the “rapidly increasing LLCC charged” through the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM), which had become a “significant financial burden” on consumers in the Visayas. In its letter to Libanan, ESAMELCO estimated that excessive LLCC charges passed on to consumers in Eastern Visayas alone, or in Region 8, had accumulated to some P1.55 billion since January this year. “The oppressive LLCC charges constitute an added burden on electricity consumers, many of whom are already struggling with rising living costs and finding it increasingly difficult to provide for the basic needs of their families,” Libanan said. “Consumers should not be made to shoulder the cost of the electricity market’s defective pricing and settlement system. If consumers were overcharged, they deserve to get their money back,” he added. LLCC, or Line Loss and Congestion Cost, is essentially the same charge referred to by the ERC as the “ line rental ” charge. The charge is meant to cover two basic costs involved in delivering electricity: power lost as electricity travels through transmission lines, and the additional cost when transmission lines become congested and cheaper electricity from another area cannot be delivered. In simple terms, LLCC is supposed to reflect the actual cost of moving electricity from where it is generated to where it is consumed. The ERC on Aug. 13 ordered corrective measures after finding that the WESM had been incorrectly calculating the congestion component of electricity prices in certain situations, resulting in Line Rental or LLCC charges that were higher than they should have been, particularly when the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) links connecting Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao became constrained. The ERC said the problem was not primarily in the formula for distributing market surpluses, but in the way the WESM pricing model computed electricity prices when the HVDC links reached their transmission limits. Instead of properly reflecting congestion as an additional cost, the ERC said the system generated separate baseline prices for the affected regions, distorting the computation of Line Rental charges. Under its order, the ERC directed the Independent Electricity Market Operator of the Philippines (IEMOP) to suspend the collection or payment of the Line Rental Trading Amount in cases where different electricity prices are generated because of constraints at HVDC interconnections or between pricing regions. The ERC also ordered a permanent correction of the pricing methodology and directed IEMOP to engage an independent auditor to recalculate the market's Net Settlement Surplus and Net Settlement Deficit allocations dating back to June 26, 2021. The audit could lead to refunds for consumers who were overcharged. IEMOP was ordered to submit a proposed methodology and timetable for refunding or collecting any resulting adjustments from affected market participants and consumers, with the adjustments potentially spread over several billing periods.

Takaichi honors Yasukuni Shrine from afar on war anniversary. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi did not visit Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine on Saturday, the 81st anniversary of the end of World War II, but worshiped toward the war-related shrine from afar before attending a national war anniversary ceremony. Takaichi also sent a cash offering from her own money in her capacity as president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party. Shortly after 11 a.m., Takaichi arrived at the parking area of the Nippon Budokan Hall, the venue of the ceremony. About 10 minutes after arrival, she exited the car, turned toward Yasukuni Shrine, and performed the traditional Shinto ritual of two bows, two claps, and one bow. Aides to the prime minister admitted that she prayed in the direction of the shrine, located a 10-minute walk from the Nippon Budokan Hall. Takaichi apparently hoped to maintain her conservative supporters, as her cabinet's approval rate has declined in recent months. The shrine is viewed by China and South Korea as a symbol of Japan's past militarism, because it enshrines Class-A war criminals alongside the war dead. Before taking office last October, Takaichi, a leading conservative hawk in the LDP, regularly visited the shrine, including when she was a cabinet minister. During the 2024 LDP leadership election, she vowed to continue visiting the shrine even if she became prime minister. However, she skipped visiting the shrine during its festivals last autumn, just before she was named prime minister, and this spring. In the 2025 party leadership election, she said that she would pray from anywhere. On Saturday, four of her cabinet ministers visited Yasukuni Shrine separately. They were Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, Hitoshi Kikawada, the minister of state for Okinawa and Northern Territories affairs, economic and fiscal policy minister Minoru Kiuchi, and economic security minister Kimi Onoda. This is the first time in six years that as many as four ministers have visited Yasukuni Shrine on the war-end anniversary. Koizumi became the first defense minister to visit the shrine on the occasion since Minoru Kihara in 2024. Kikawada and Kiuchi told reporters separately that they prayed for peace for the souls enshrined there, while Koizumi and Onoda did not respond to reporters. Still, Koizumi wrote on X, formerly Twitter, that he renewed his determination to continue Japan's pursuit of peace. LDP Secretary-General Shunichi Suzuki, who delivered Takaichi's offering, also visited the shrine, along with Haruko Arimura, head of the party's General Council, and Yasutoshi Nishimura, the party's election campaign chief. Suzuki later told reporters that he respected the prime minister's thoughts about the enshrined souls. He also said that his visit demonstrated the LDP's policy of "continuing visits to Yasukuni Shrine." The day's other visitors included LDP Executive Acting Secretary-General Koichi Hagiuda, Sanseito party leader Sohei Kamiya, and Conservative Party of Japan head Naoki Hyakuta. A suprapartisan group of about 90 lawmakers, including members of the LDP and its coalition party, the Japan Innovation Party, visited the shrine together. The Chinese Foreign Ministry issued a spokesperson's statement strongly protesting Takaichi's offering and the four ministers' visit to Yasukuni Shrine. A spokesperson for the South Korean Foreign Ministry also released a statement criticizing the actions by Takaichi and the ministers as anachronistic and ignorant of history.

Villanueva to DOLE: Consider interim assistance to workers while P85 wage hike is in limbo. Senator Joel Villanueva on Sunday, August 16 called on the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to consider granting interim assistance to the workers affected by the injunction order on the P85-wage increase while the dispute is still unresolved. Villanueva made the call as he expressed disappointment on the Pasig City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 152’s granting of a writ of preliminary injunction that would further delay the implementation of the P85-wage hike for workers. The preliminary injunction was sought by construction companies Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. and R-II Builders on July 23. The court’s 14-page order also set a bond of P10-billion. Villanueva, who heads the Senate labor and employment panel, said he continues to stand with the National Wages and Productivity Commission and the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-NCR in defending the integrity of the wage-setting process. “Republic Act No. 6727 built this tripartite system more than three decades ago, and it has balanced the competing interests of labor, management, and government ever since. That system exists precisely so that wage adjustments are worked out at the negotiating table based on social and economic realities on the ground, not in a courtroom,” Villanueva said. “The law is explicit on this point: Article 126 of the Labor Code bars any court from issuing an injunction or restraining order against the proceedings of the NWPC or the Regional Boards. Any party aggrieved by a wage order has a clear administrative remedy, which is to appeal to the NWPC and that is the venue where this dispute belongs,” the senator reiterated. “What our wage-setting process needs right now is robust negotiation within the social dialogue framework, not a fight that gets dragged into politics or into the courts. Tripartism works because labor, management, and government sit down and hash it out through the RTWPB. When that process gets short-circuited by litigation outside its proper venue, it is workers who absorb the uncertainty while the case drags on,” he stressed. Villanueva pointed out Filipino workers—especially minimum wage earners—"cannot afford to wait on the sidelines” while the legal controversies surrounding the injunction are sorted out in the courts. “While the relief brought about by the wage adjustment is on hold, prices of basic goods such as food and fuel continue to rise beyond our control, making current wage levels no longer sufficient for workers to live decently,” he noted. “We appeal to the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to look into interim assistance measures for minimum wage earners in the NCR while the implementation of the wage order remains in limbo,” he urged. “Workers should not have to bear the cost of a legal question that is not of their making,” the senator reiterated. “We, likewise, reiterate our full support for the NWPC and RTWPB-NCR as they pursue the appropriate legal remedies with the Office of the Solicitor General. It is the wage-setting mechanism, not litigation, that should settle this matter,” he further stated.

US pulls last aircraft carrier in Asia as Trump focuses on Iran and the Western Hemisphere. WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's war against Iran is stretching the limits of U.S. aircraft carriers and leaving the western Pacific without one of the key American warships as China shows more signs of aggression. The USS George Washington is departing the Pacific and expected to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East amid growing concerns about mental health and supply issues aboard the long-deployed carrier. The Lincoln has had its time at sea extended from its original May return date to support operations against Iran. The lack of a U.S. carrier in the Pacific may be short-lived if the Navy deploys another in the next couple of months. But it shows how the open-ended operations with Iran are running some American sailors ragged, analysts say, while the Trump administration further retreats from the Asia-Pacific region and focuses on the Western Hemisphere. “The administration says that the Pacific is supposed to be the most important behind the Western Hemisphere,” said Greg Poling, director of the Southeast Asia Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Instead, the U.S. is "doing the exact opposite" of its previously expressed goal of pulling out of the Middle East. American allies in the Pacific are unsettled over the unpredictability of the Republican administration, Poling said, while Beijing “is quite happy with U.S. distraction, with the frustration of U.S. allies and partners." China may take advantage of US carrier's absence Beijing sees the U.S. military presence in the region as a threat to China’s rise and an obstacle to its ambition to seize Taiwan, the self-governing island it claims as its own. But the United States has argued that the Pacific region is too important economically to lose. No one expects China to invade Taiwan because an American aircraft carrier has left the region.
